The test lists exactly nine conversations: {{PARENT}} (slug {{PARENT_SLUG}}), updated at that moment, with 8 subagents, and its subagents older-subagent-0 to older-subagent-7, updated one or two days before; the live update stream is cut off. The picker's buttons "Previous day", "Next day", "Today" and "Turn off Daily" are {"selector": "[data-testid='conversation-day-filter']", "role": "button", "name": "...", "exact": true}. To "group by L": click the button "View options", then click {"selector": ".group-by-menu", "role": "button", "name": "L", "exact": true}. Conversation rows are ".conversation-item[data-conversation-id='<id>']" ("the row of <id>"). Every selector you need is given here, so do not explore the source code or read other tests (the old Playwright spec is being replaced and does not apply): write all the steps in one run_steps call right away, and look something up only if a step fails. Perform the numbered steps in order, each fully. A button "X" is {"role": "button", "name": "X", "exact": true}, with a "selector" to scope it when it is a row's, a menu's or a group's; but "there is no button X" counts {"role": "button", "name": "X"} without exact, so that a name containing X counts too. Texts that "are exactly [...]" are checked with assert_texts. "There is no S", "no S" or "none" means no element matches at all: assert_count 0, never a visibility check.
